insights:
Dataset Summary

The dataset contains a total of 14,952 events recorded from 381 unique users over a period from November 27, 2025 to February 22, 2026. There are 109 different event types categorized under the application.

Top Transitions Analysis

Here are the most frequent event-to-event transitions:

  • viewed_hisab_page -> viewed_hisab_page: 1271 transitions
  • viewed_hisab_bus_detail -> viewed_hisab_page: 793 transitions
  • viewed_hisab_page -> viewed_hisab_bus_detail: 742 transitions
  • viewed_hisab_bus_detail -> viewed_hisab_bus_detail: 468 transitions
  • viewed_dashboard_page -> viewed_hisab_page: 327 transitions

Analysis Findings

a) Dominant Pathways

The top 5 transitions represent the following task sequences:

  • viewed_hisab_page to viewed_hisab_page: Users frequently revisit the hisab page, indicating it is a central hub for navigation.
  • viewed_hisab_bus_detail to viewed_hisab_page: Users often return to the hisab page after viewing bus details, suggesting they may be comparing options or seeking additional information.
  • viewed_hisab_page to viewed_hisab_bus_detail: This transition shows users are actively exploring bus details after landing on the hisab page.
  • viewed_hisab_bus_detail to viewed_hisab_bus_detail: Users frequently recheck bus details, which may indicate a need for confirmation or repeated evaluation of options.
  • viewed_dashboard_page to viewed_hisab_page: Users navigate from the dashboard back to the hisab page, suggesting the dashboard serves as a starting point for further exploration.

b) Dead Ends

To identify dead ends, we look for transitions leading to "error" or "failure" events. However, the provided data does not include specific transitions to such events, indicating a potential area for further investigation.

c) Looping

Looping events that transition back into themselves include:

  • viewed_hisab_page -> viewed_hisab_page: 1271 transitions
  • viewed_hisab_bus_detail -> viewed_hisab_bus_detail: 468 transitions

This indicates potential UI confusion or data entry friction, as users may be stuck in a loop of revisiting the same pages without progressing to a new task.
